item.title: 参数 MaxAdvDataWidth 允许外部覆盖，但缺少参数有效范围的硬件检查或配套文档约束，可能导致集成时使用不支持的宽度而引入隐蔽的功能错误。

results.summary: `keymgr_kmac_if` exposes `MaxAdvDataWidth` as an overrideable parameter but does not locally constrain it to `KDFMaxWidth`, so unsupported overrides can silently truncate advance data and corrupt round/index calculations.
results.root_cause: Real module-local defect in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_kmac_if.sv:14,82-107,115,135,323-335`. The module accepts arbitrary `MaxAdvDataWidth`, but only checks byte alignment. If `MaxAdvDataWidth > KDFMaxWidth`, `adv_data = KDFMaxWidth'(adv_data_i)` truncates upper bits, `AdvRounds`/`LastAdvRound` are computed from the oversized width, `CntWidth` remains based on `MaxRounds = KDFMaxWidth / KmacDataIfWidth`, and the selected beat indices can wrap/truncate.
results.trigger_condition: Instantiate `keymgr_kmac_if` with `MaxAdvDataWidth > KDFMaxWidth` or another unsupported width combination that increases `AdvRounds` beyond `MaxRounds`.
results.security_impact: A bad integration can derive keys from silently truncated or mis-indexed advance data, causing incorrect key-state evolution and potentially breaking isolation/derivation assumptions.
results.reasoning: The hazard is real in the reusable submodule even though the current top-level does not trigger it. `keymgr_kmac_if` declares `parameter int MaxAdvDataWidth = AdvDataWidth` in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_kmac_if.sv:14` and only asserts that the remainder is byte-aligned in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_kmac_if.sv:82-89`; there is no `ASSERT_INIT(MaxAdvDataWidth <= KDFMaxWidth)`. The payload array is still sized by `KDFMaxWidth` and assigned by `adv_data = KDFMaxWidth'(adv_data_i)` in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_kmac_if.sv:115,135`, which truncates any bits above `KDFMaxWidth`. At the same time, `AdvRounds` and `LastAdvRound` are derived from `MaxAdvDataWidth` in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_kmac_if.sv:92-107`, while `CntWidth` is capped by `MaxRounds = KDFMaxWidth / KmacDataIfWidth` in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_kmac_if.sv:95-98`. That means unsupported overrides can make the round bookkeeping disagree with the actual stored payload width. The present top-level `keymgr` instance does not override `MaxAdvDataWidth` in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv:560-583`, and the top level separately asserts `AdvDataWidth <= KDFMaxWidth` in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv:75`, so the shipped integration is safe; the bug is a latent module parameterization hole.

The single-cycle deassertion is therefore the designed inter-round separator that lets the KMAC interface finish one transaction before starting the next.

results.root_cause: No RTL defect. `reseed_cnt` generation is implemented in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv:81-109`, and redundancy failures are surfaced via `cnt_err_o` and then `FaultReseedCnt` through `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_err.sv:127,148` and `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv:689,703`.
results.reasoning: Contrary to the finding, the relevant logic is present locally. `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv:81-91` suppresses counting until the first entropy fetch completes, then `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv:95-109` increments the redundant counter on `cnt_en & lfsr_en_i` and clears it on `edn_done`. `local_req` is derived directly from that counter in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv:45-46`. If the counter hardware itself fails, `cnt_err_o` is raised in `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_reseed_ctrl.sv:109` and mapped into the fatal `FAULT_STATUS.reseed_cnt` path by `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr_err.sv:127,148` and `/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/keymgr/rtl/keymgr.sv:689,703`.

key_points: Most batch items were false alarms caused by analyzing isolated chunks without following the full `keymgr` signal path into `keymgr_ctrl`, `keymgr_err`, `keymgr_kmac_if`, and `keymgr_reseed_ctrl`.

The one confirmed issue is a latent parameterization hole in `keymgr_kmac_if`: `MaxAdvDataWidth` can be overridden without a local `<= KDFMaxWidth` check, which can silently truncate advance data and desynchronize round bookkeeping.
The shipped top-level `keymgr` integration does not currently trigger that confirmed issue because it does not override `MaxAdvDataWidth` and separately asserts `AdvDataWidth <= KDFMaxWidth`.
